**Voica v0.10.0 — your clipboard, left alone.**

### The clipboard can be given back

A dictation is inserted by pasting, so until now it replaced whatever you had copied: copy a link,
dictate, press Ctrl+V — and get the dictation instead of the link
([#2](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/issues/2)).

There is now a switch for it: **Settings → Dictation → Keep the dictation in the clipboard**. It is
**on by default**, which is how Voica has always behaved. Turn it **off**, and the clipboard is only
borrowed for the paste — half a second later, what you had copied is back.

- **Text, links, formatted text, files and images** come back exactly as they were.
- If you **copy something new** in that half second, it is left alone.
- The dictation **does not appear in clipboard history** (Win+V) or cloud sync.
- In a **remote-desktop** window the return waits five seconds, so the paste has time to travel.
- Contents that cannot be kept — over 64 MB, an e-mail attachment, a program that is not responding —
  are not touched: the dictation stays in the clipboard, as before, and the notification says so.

### What it cannot do

There is no way to insert text into another program's field without the clipboard, short of typing
it key by key — which misbehaves in a different way in every application. So the clipboard is still
used, briefly, and one thing does not come back: **the program you copied from stops treating the
contents as its own.**

- **Excel** leaves its copy mode (the dashed outline disappears) and then pastes **values instead of
  formulas**, with a warning.
- **Word** pastes its own text by the *Pasting from other programs* setting. The default there,
  *Merge Formatting*, keeps tables and bold but drops colours and sizes; *Keep Source Formatting*
  keeps everything.

This is how Windows works, not something Voica can fix — which is why the old behaviour stays the
default and giving the clipboard back is your choice. Either way it beats what happens today, when a
dictation leaves nothing of your copy at all.

Any dictation can always be copied again from **History**.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.10.0.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Installing over an existing copy keeps your history, settings and API key.

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
